title: Relative reductive centre as a torus weight kernel
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-group scheme is an $S$-scheme with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams, as in [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. A reductive $S$-group is a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] group whose geometric fibres are connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] and have no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup. Unipotent means that in a faithful matrix representation every geometric point is a unipotent matrix. The centre $Z(G)$ is the subgroup functor of points commuting with all points after every algebra extension. A torus over $S$ is an $S$-group scheme which, locally for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of $S$, is isomorphic to a finite product of copies of $\mathbf G_{m}$. A maximal torus is a closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] which is a torus over $S$ and which on every geometric fibre is maximal among subgroups isomorphic to a product of multiplicative groups; $\mathbf G_{m,S}=\operatorname{Spec}A[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. Let $G$ be reductive. Its centre is represented by a closed subgroup scheme of multiplicative type, meaning a form, locally for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings, of $D_A(N)=\operatorname{Spec}A[N]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $N$ [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. It is flat over $S$, and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change. If $T\subseteq G$ is a maximal torus, the centre, as a subgroup of $T$, is the scheme-theoretic kernel of the conjugation action of $T$ on $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$; the latter is the tangent module with its full torus coaction [lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change]. In particular, suppose $T=D_A(M)$, $M=\mathbf Z^r$, and $\Phi\subset M\setminus\{0\}$ is a finite set such that at every geometric point of $S$ the nonzero weights of this action are exactly $\Phi$. For $m\in M$, let $\chi_m:T\to\mathbf G_{m,S}$ be the character with coordinate $e_m$. Then $Z(G)=\bigcap_{m\in\Phi}\ker\chi_m=D_A(M/\mathbf Z\Phi)$ inside $T$, where $\mathbf Z\Phi$ is the subgroup generated by $\Phi$. The equality is scheme-theoretic and commutes with arbitrary base change, including to nonreduced rings. Empty $\Phi$ is allowed.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.4 and its weight-decomposition proof, printed pp.98--100; Corollary 3.3.6(1), printed p.101. Constant-support character formula also in Example 5.1.7, printed p.138. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag supplies this relative reductive-group theorem.

proof.text: First arrange a finite affine fppf covering on which a split maximal torus exists. At a geometric point choose a maximal torus by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Lift its parametrized inclusion by [lem-sfb-geometric-torus-fppf-lift], and restrict its affine source around the marked point using [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-fibre-openness] so that it is maximal on every geometric fibre there. These restrictions can be chosen affine. The covering morphisms are flat of finite presentation, and their images are open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Their images cover $S$; quasi-compactness from [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] gives a finite subcover. Their finite disjoint union exists by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] and is affine: for finitely many affine components its coordinate ring is their product, as the orthogonal idempotents show. Thus it is a single faithfully flat affine cover. The source rings are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. The original affine finite-type group is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]; smoothness persists by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). We now work on one such affine patch with $T=D_A(M)$, $M=\mathbf Z^r$.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.4, beginning of proof, printed pp.98--99; local split maximal torus via Proposition 3.1.6 and Proposition 3.1.9. The finite affine refinement is written out.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change], $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ has a finite-support decomposition into finite projective weight modules $\mathfrak g_m$, with arbitrary-base-change compatibility. By [lem-sfb-relative-torus-bundle-weights], after a Zariski refinement the ranks of all these finitely many summands are constant. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free], refine once more so they are free. Write $\Phi$ for the nonzero characters whose summands have positive rank on the patch. This uses full character weights, so a character divisible by the residue characteristic is not discarded. The zero weight contributes no equation to a trivial-action condition. The resulting refinements are finite affine covers, using quasi-compactness as in step 1.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.4, weight decomposition and constant-rank localization, printed p.99.

proof.text: Put $L=\mathbf Z\Phi\subseteq M$ and $H=D_A(M/L)\hookrightarrow T$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality] to the character map $\mathbf Z^{\Phi}\to M$ sending the basis vector at $m$ to $m$: its dual is the tuple $(\chi_m)_{m\in\Phi}$, and its kernel is $H=\bigcap_{m\in\Phi}\ker\chi_m$. This is a closed subgroup and the formula commutes with arbitrary base change. The group algebra $A[M/L]$ is free on the elements of $M/L$. Tensoring an injection with it is the direct sum of copies of that injection, and hence injective, so it is flat by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] makes $H\to S$ flat. For every $A$-algebra $B$, an element $t\in T(B)$ acts on $B\otimes_A\mathfrak g_m$ by the scalar $\chi_m(t)$. On each nonzero free summand identity action is equivalent to $\chi_m(t)=1$, checked on a basis vector. Thus $H_B$ is exactly the kernel of the $T_B$-action on $\operatorname{Lie}(G_B)$, for every $B$, and it acts trivially on that module. No reducedness of $B$ or freeness of $M/L$ is used.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.4, construction of H, printed p.99; Appendix B.1 and Example 5.1.7, printed p.138.

proof.text: Let $C=C_G(H)$. By [lem-sfb-split-diagonalizable-centralizer-smooth], $C$ is a smooth affine finitely presented closed subgroup and $\operatorname{Lie}(C_B)=\operatorname{Lie}(G_B)^{H_B}$. Step 3 makes this all of $\operatorname{Lie}(G_B)$. Over each algebraically closed geometric residue field $k$, the tangent map $C_k\hookrightarrow G_k$ is therefore an isomorphism at the identity. Translation by each point of $C_k(k)$ makes it an isomorphism at every such point. By [lem-sfb-smooth-tangent-isomorphism-etale] this closed immersion is etale, and by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-closed-immersion-open] it is also open. Its image is nonempty, open and closed in the connected $G_k$, so $C_k=G_k$. The isomorphism on a geometric fibre descends to its residue-field fibre by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-isomorphism], applied to the faithfully flat field extension. To conclude over $A$, apply [lem-sfb-fibrewise-flatness-criterion] to $C\hookrightarrow G$ over $S$: $C/S$ is locally finitely presented and flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], $G/S$ is locally finite type, and the fibre maps are isomorphisms, hence flat. Consequently $C\hookrightarrow G$ is flat and is surjective since every geometric fibre is surjective. Now [lem-sfb-surjective-flat-closed-immersion-isomorphism] gives $C=G$. This proves $H$ central scheme-theoretically, and the equality persists under every base change.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.4, centralizer argument, printed p.99; Lemma 2.2.4. Agent supplies the fibrewise-flatness proof of the global equality.

proof.text: The same centralizer lemma [lem-sfb-split-diagonalizable-centralizer-smooth], now with $K=T$, gives a smooth affine finitely presented $C_G(T)$ whose formation commutes with arbitrary base change. On every geometric fibre, [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer] says $T_k=C_{G_k}(T_k)$ scheme-theoretically. This equality descends to each residue-field fibre by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-isomorphism]. The inclusion $T\hookrightarrow C_G(T)$ is closed: its ideal is the image in the coordinate ring of $C_G(T)$ of the ideal defining $T$ in $G$. Both source and target are smooth over $S$, so [lem-pc-smooth-flat] and [lem-sfb-fibrewise-flatness-criterion] make this inclusion flat. It is surjective on fibres, hence surjective. By [lem-sfb-surjective-flat-closed-immersion-isomorphism], $C_G(T)=T$. This relative equality, including on nonreduced test algebras, remains valid after arbitrary base change.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.4, use of the self-centralizer of T, printed p.99; Proposition 3.1.9(2).

proof.text: For any $A$-algebra $B$, a central point $g\in G(B)$ centralizes $T$ after every extension, so step 5 puts it in $T(B)$. Conjugation by $g$ is the identity morphism of $G_B$; applying it to dual-number points shows its action on $\operatorname{Lie}(G_B)$ is the identity. Step 3 then gives $g\in H(B)$. Conversely step 4 says that every $H(B)$-point commutes with every point of $G$ after every $B$-algebra extension. Thus $H$ represents the centre functor. This argument applies also to the group after any $A\to B$, since steps 3--5 already hold there: $Z(G_B)=H_B$. In particular these identifications are natural for successive base changes. This is equality of subgroup functors on all algebras, rather than an inference from equality of geometric points.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.4, central points lie in H, printed p.99.

proof.text: On overlaps of the affine fppf patches of steps 1--2, the constructed subgroups both represent the same central subfunctor by step 6, so their identifications as subfunctors of $G$ give a descent datum satisfying the cocycle identity. Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-affine-descent-effective] to this datum to obtain a scheme $Z/S$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-affine] to see $Z/S$ is affine. The local inclusions into $G$, and local group operations, descend by [lem-galois-fpqc-morphisms-descend]; their diagrams hold globally because that node also gives uniqueness. By base changing the cover to $G$, using [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms](3), and applying [lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion], the descended inclusion $Z\to G$ is closed. On each test scheme, factorization of a central section through $Z$ can be checked on this cover and the local factorizations glue uniquely by [lem-galois-fpqc-morphisms-descend]. Therefore $Z$ represents the centre. In applying affine effectivity the cover is a single affine fpqc morphism: the finite affine refinements were consolidated by the finite-product construction in step 1.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.4, effective affine descent, printed p.98. Stacks Tags 0245 (lemma-affine), 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms), 02L5, 02L6 and 022D give the general descent tools.

proof.text: By step 3 every local centre is $D_A(M/L)$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M/L$. Thus $Z$ is of multiplicative type with exactly the fppf-local meaning in the statement. Its local flatness in step 3 descends by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-flat]. For an arbitrary $S'\to S$, pull back the cover, which is fpqc by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms](3). On each resulting patch step 6 identifies the base-changed $Z$ with the centre of the base-changed group, even when the new ring is nonreduced or non-Noetherian. Factorizations of sections and their uniqueness descend by [lem-galois-fpqc-morphisms-descend], so $Z\times_SS'=Z(G\times_SS')$ as closed subgroup schemes. The identifications are the ones induced by the inclusion in $G$, hence agree under successive base changes.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.4, descent and base change of the reductive centre, printed pp.98--99; Stacks Tags 02L2 and 022D.

proof.text: For any given maximal torus $T\subseteq G$, work fppf-locally where it is split, as allowed by the definition of a torus. Refine by affine finite-presentation covering patches and the constant-rank weight patches of step 2. Over these patches the argument of steps 3--6 used only that this particular $T$ is fibrewise maximal, and proves that the centre is contained in $T$ and is the kernel of its action on $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$. Descent of morphisms and their equality from [lem-galois-fpqc-morphisms-descend] gives the global containment and equality of kernel subfunctors. If already $T=D_A(M)$ and the geometric nonzero weights are the fixed set $\Phi$, the weight modules outside $\Phi\cup\{0\}$ have rank zero at every prime and so vanish, while each $m\in\Phi$ has positive rank at every prime, by [lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-rank-locally-constant]. Locally freeing these summands by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free], the basis calculation of step 3 gives precisely the equations $\chi_m=1$ for $m\in\Phi$. Hence their common kernel is $D_A(M/\mathbf Z\Phi)$ by [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality], with arbitrary-base-change compatibility. For $\Phi=\varnothing$, there are no equations and this is $D_A(M)=T$; the proof also allows $r=0$.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.6(1), printed p.101, and Example 5.1.7, printed p.138; explicit constant-support variant.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N6-69792f027 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 9 steps and the new node in full, plus the statement of every one of the 30 proof_deps. The item statement is unchanged. Tests: empty Φ gives T; r=0; SL_2 over Z gives μ_2, nonreduced over F_2; GL_n gives G_m. Step-by-step checks: steps 1-2 build a finite affine fppf cover with a split torus that is maximal on every geometric fibre (lift node, openness node, flat-lfp-open, quasi-compactness), with Noetherian nonzero patches and free weight summands of constant rank. Step 3 gets H=D(M/ZΦ) as the kernel from character-duality applied to Z^Φ→M; H is flat because its algebra is free; on free summands of positive rank H is exactly the kernel of the action. Step 4 applies the new centralizer node to H: the Lie algebra is invariant, so the map is an isomorphism on tangent spaces; it is then étale, open, and an isomorphism on connected geometric fibres; this descends to residue fields; the fibrewise-flatness criterion and the closed-immersion criterion give C_G(H)=G. All hypotheses of the cited nodes check. Step 5 gets C_G(T)=T the same way, via the field self-centralizer node and base change. Step 6 is a genuine elementary check. Steps 7-8 descend correctly (affine effectivity, affineness, morphism and closed-immersion descent, flatness) and get base change through step 6. Step 9 treats a non-split torus and the constant-Φ formula through ranks. New node lem-sfb-split-diagonalizable-centralizer-smooth: it is the split case of Conrad Lemma 2.2.4 and is true. Tests: N=0 gives G; μ_p inside SL_p in char p gives SL_p; diag(ζ,1) inside GL_2 over F_p gives the diagonal torus, whose Lie algebra is the full-action invariants. It is statement-only and self-contained. It is not a duplicate: relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer covers only split tori; mu-n-fixed needs the action to extend to G_m; the torus-fixed and Lie nodes are over fields. It is not a clause of the item. Source: Conrad is not in literature/, so the worker filed WANTED and marked proof_origin.by=agent, as brief-stage1 l.66 requires; I checked against the standard theorem (Conrad Thm 3.3.4 / Cor 3.3.6(1)). Batch-5: all six trf nodes reached (fppf-covering-base-change, artin-approximation, finite-type-component-open-qc, fppf-is-fpqc, localization-finite-presentation, split-lattice-torus-projection) are generic sk-i-curve-zero tools, not steps of the proof of the trace formula or of Poincare duality, so they are accepted.
